US-119-HR10908.title: Ending Patient Runaround Act

actions.text: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committee on Ways and Means, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
Introduced in House

US-119-HR10908.description: To implement Universal Savings Accounts and expand transparency, competition, and patient rights in health care.
US-119-HR10908.aiSummary: The bill would create Universal Savings Accounts with tax rules for deposits, withdrawals, and extra contributions. It would also require health plans and insurers to give prior approval decisions in writing and through a secure portal within 30 days, and to share procedure codes, prices, and covered services with insurance contracts. It would bar some changes to drug tiers or covered services during a plan term and would set rules tied to in-network and out-of-network provider payments.

US-119-HR10809.title: Make Data Centers Pay Act

actions.text: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
Introduced in House

US-119-HR10809.description: To amend the Federal Power Act to protect ratepayers from costs relating to the electric loads of data centers and high-density computing facilities.
US-119-HR10809.aiSummary: The bill would change federal power law so large data centers and high-density computing sites must pay the full added electric costs they cause. Those costs could not be passed on to other utility customers, and utilities would have to get financial backing before building or upgrading power equipment for these sites. The rules would apply to new covered loads, which are sites using at least 20 megawatts of power, while older approved arrangements would stay in place.

US-119-S5648.description: A bill to direct agencies to be transparent when using automated and augmented systems to interact with the public or make critical decisions, and for other purposes.
US-119-S5648.aiSummary: The bill would direct federal agencies to be open about when they use automated systems and AI to interact with the public or help make important decisions. It would require public lists of those systems, plain-language notices to people, a way to appeal adverse decisions, and guidance on privacy, civil rights, and public input. It would also set rules for chatbots and similar tools, including notice when someone is talking to an automated system and a way to reach a human worker.

US-119-S5604.title: Improving Species Recovery Act

actions.text: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Environment and Public Works.
Introduced in Senate

US-119-S5604.description: A bill to amend the Endangered Species Act of 1973 to make improvements to that Act, and for other purposes.
US-119-S5604.aiSummary: The bill would change the Endangered Species Act by setting clearer standards for how the Fish and Wildlife Service considers conservation steps before listing a species as threatened or endangered. It would also require more detail on species status and recovery plans, add rules for how voluntary conservation actions are considered when removing a species from the list, and expand online tools to speed up agency consultations. The measure would affect the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, other agencies that work under the act, and states, landowners, and others involved in species conservation.

US-119-S3404.description: A bill to require a report on Federal support to the cybersecurity of commercial satellite systems, and for other purposes.
US-119-S3404.aiSummary: The bill would require a federal study and report on how the government supports cybersecurity for commercial satellite systems. It would also direct the Commerce Department to create a public online clearinghouse with cybersecurity resources and voluntary guidance, including help for small businesses. The bill would also call for a strategy on sharing information and setting roles among federal agencies and private companies.

US-119-S3723.description: A bill to require the Secretary of the Interior to conduct a study to determine the feasibility of constructing a project to supply municipal, rural, and industrial water from the Missouri River to the Western Dakota Regional Water System, and for other purposes.
US-119-S3723.aiSummary: The bill would require the Secretary of the Interior to study whether a project could bring water from the Missouri River to the Western Dakota Regional Water System for homes, farms, and industry. The study would be done with the local water group, and the Secretary would later report on whether the project is technically and financially workable and whether it should be built. It would cap federal spending on the study at $10 million, with the federal share limited to no more than half.

US-119-HJRES60.title: Providing for congressional disapproval under chapter 8 of title 5, United States Code, of the rule submitted by the National Park Service relating to "Glen Canyon National Recreation Area: Motor Vehicles".
US-119-HJRES60.summary:
This joint resolution allows off-road vehicles to be used in certain areas of the Glen Canyon National Recreation Area, which is in northern Arizona and southeastern Utah and contains Lake Powell.

Specifically, the joint resolution nullifies the rule issued by the National Park Service (NPS) titled Glen Canyon National Recreation Area; Motor Vehicles and published on January 13, 2025. Under the rule, the NPS limited the use of off-road vehicles, such as off-highway vehicles and all-terrain vehicles, in certain areas. For instance, the rule prohibited the use of off-road vehicles on an 8-mile segment of the Poison Spring Loop located on Route 633 proceeding north to Route 730 in the Orange Cliffs Special Management Unit. The rule also eliminated the authority of the NPS to open the upper portion of the Flint Trail in that unit to off-road vehicles. Additionally, the rule limited off-road vehicle use from certain roads to the shoreline of the lake.

US-119-HJRES60.aiSummary: This joint resolution became law and cancels a National Park Service rule on motor vehicles in the Glen Canyon National Recreation Area. It allows off-road vehicles in certain areas of the park, including parts of the Orange Cliffs Special Management Unit. The park area is in northern Arizona and southeastern Utah and includes Lake Powell.
